decisions.description: Withdrawals are capped at 5000.00 per account per day, a limit the plan never mentions.
The daily withdrawal counter is never reset, so the 'daily' limit is really a lifetime limit per ledger instance.
The daily limit counts only the withdrawn amount, not the fee.
The withdrawal fee is capped at a maximum of 25.00, which the plan does not specify.
The 1% withdrawal fee is rounded up to the next cent rather than to the nearest cent.
The fee is computed on the amount after rounding it to cents.
No overdraft: a withdrawal is rejected unless the balance covers both the amount and the fee.
Transfers and split payments are rejected if the sender's balance would go negative.
When a withdrawal is both over balance and over the daily limit, insufficient funds is reported first.
Transfers and split payments carry no fee; only withdrawals are charged.
Any operation on an unknown account silently creates it with a zero balance, including withdrawals, transfer sources and recipients.
Querying an unknown account returns balance 0 and an empty history instead of an error.
A repeated transaction id returns success without re-checking that the amount, accounts or operation type match the original.
Transaction ids are unique globally across all accounts and operation types, and are kept forever in memory.
Input validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with an invalid amount is rejected even if the id was already accepted.
A rejected operation does not consume its transaction id, so the same id can later succeed.
A small epsilon (1e-7) is added before rounding to cents to compensate for floating-point error.
A deposit, withdrawal or transfer of a positive amount that rounds to 0 cents (e.g. 0.004) is accepted and recorded as a zero entry.
There is no maximum amount, and non-finite values like Infinity pass the positive-number check.
Balances and history amounts are exposed as floating-point currency units rather than integer cents.
Foreign deposits use half-away-from-zero rounding (same as other amounts) instead of half-to-even.
A foreign deposit requires a positive exchange rate and is rejected as too small if it converts to 0 cents.
A foreign deposit is recorded as a plain deposit without the original currency, amount or rate.
In a split, leftover cents go one each to the first recipients in list order.
A split with no recipients is rejected; duplicate recipients and the sender among recipients are allowed.
Interest is rounded down (floor) to the cent.
Interest rate is taken as a percent, must be positive (zero rejected), and days may be fractional.
When interest rounds to zero or the balance is negative, the call succeeds but nothing is recorded and the transaction id is not consumed.
Interest is simple (not compounded) on the balance at the moment of the call.
History stores debits as positive amounts, distinguished only by the entry kind, and a withdrawal entry includes the fee.
